Subject: Deployment mode follow-up (HIPAA/BAA evidence + next steps)

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum on Elara Health's deployment qualification. High-level notes from today's discovery:

- Primary requirement: PHI workloads for a triage/chat assistant and clinical note summarization.
- Compliance bar: HIPAA with a signed BAA, SOC 2 Type II evidence preferred.
- Deployment mode being evaluated: hosted API (fastest), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) — Elara leaning toward Dedicated or Private for isolation and customer-managed keys.

What I promised to share:
1) Draft BAA for your legal/security review (attached).
2) Our most recent SOC 2 Type II report (we'll attach the redacted PDF).
3) Short answers to the deployment questions you raised (KMS, audit logs, data residency).
4) Proposed next step: schedule a 60-min security deep-dive with our Solutions Engineering team to walk the architecture and controls.

Requested items from Elara (to help us finalize recommended deployment mode):
- Which specific audit controls or evidence you need (e.g., encryption key management, access review cadence, log retention window).
- Any procurement timelines / internal deadlines (so we align dates).

Attachments: BAA_draft_Redwood.docx (draft), Redwood_Security_Summary.pdf (overview).

Proposed timeline:
- Security deep-dive week of Nov 9
- Internal review of BAA / SOC2 by Nov 12
- Procurement kickoff by Nov 20 if controls align

If Dedicated or Private are preferred, we’ll include a short tech checklist for the Solutions Engs (network peering, customer-managed KMS options, VPC egress controls).

Can you confirm times that work for the security deep-dive next week? I’ve tentatively proposed Tue Nov 9 11:00am PT with Dylan and Rishi on our side.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from our security and procurement teams before the deep-dive:

1) SOC 2: Is the SOC 2 Type II report for the current calendar year (2026) and does it cover your hosted API, dedicated, and private control plane services? We need scope cleared for any environment that will process PHI.
2) KMS/Keys: For Dedicated deployments, do you support customer-managed keys (CMK)? For Private/VPC, can customers retain sole control (BYOK/HSM)? Please call out encryption at rest & in transit, and key rotation policies.
3) Audit logs & retention: Where are tenant audit logs stored, what retention windows exist by default, and can we export to our SIEM?
4) Data deletion/ERASURE: Standard SLA for data deletion and proof of deletion for terminated data sets.
5) Subprocessors: current list and any planned changes in next 90 days.

We have an internal security questionnaire that we typically send; I’ve attached the first pass (Elara_Security_Questionnaire_v1.docx). Filling it out will help us map requirements to deployment options.

Timing/ops: Nov 9 at 11:00am PT works for a preliminary deep-dive for us — I'll confirm with our security lead and send an invite if everyone is available.

Thanks again — if you can attach the SOC2 PDF and a short note (1–2 bullets) on KMS and retention that would help pre-seed the call.

Jane — thanks for the fast response and the questionnaire. I’m attaching the items you asked for and answering your bullets below to help the security review:

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (redacted), BAA_draft_Redwood.docx, Redwood_KMS_and_Logging_FAQ.pdf

Questions/answers (short):
1) SOC 2: Our most recent SOC 2 Type II report is the 2026 report (coverage period Jan–Dec 2025, issued Aug 2026). Scope includes the Redwood control plane, hosted API endpoints, and Dedicated control interfaces; Private on-prem deployments are out of scope (customer-managed), but our partnering deployable control plane components are documented in the report. We’ve attached the redacted PDF.

2) KMS/Keys:
- Private VPC/on-prem: full BYOK support; customers can use their HSM/KMS and retain sole key custody.
- Dedicated: we support customer-managed keys for encryption at rest on Dedicated capacity in our enterprise plans (requires a short onboarding + KMS integration).
- Hosted API: keys are managed by Redwood by default; we can discuss additional controls and tokenization patterns if Hosted is considered.
- All traffic is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3) and data at rest is AES-256. Key rotation policies and rotation windows are documented in the attached KMS FAQ.

3) Audit logs & retention:
- Default: 90-day retention for request/response audit logs in Hosted and Dedicated.
- Extended retention: add-on up to 3 years (exportable).
- Exports: logs can be streamed to your SIEM via secure syslog/S3 export or pulled via our audit log API.

4) Data deletion:
- Standard deletion request processed within 30 days; we provide deletion receipts for the primary processing copies. For Dedicated/Private we can accommodate shorter windows per contract.

5) Subprocessors: I’ve included a link in the attached security summary listing current subprocessors; there are no planned changes in the next 90 days.

Next steps we propose:
- 60-min security deep-dive on Tue Nov 9 at 11:00am PT (Dylan will cover architecture & KMS details; Rishi will join for compliance questions). Please send a calendar invite and include your security lead.
- We’ll fill the questionnaire you attached prior to the call and send it back 24 hours in advance.
- Legal: we’ve attached a draft BAA for review; happy to take redlines in DocuSign or Word.

If that timeline works, I’ll have Dylan and I prepare a 15-min architecture walkthrough + 35-min controls/Q&A for the call.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
